sense: of a whole country or people

terms.gloss: of the state or the whole people: national, as against private or local
evidence: Caes. BG 6.13.4: sacrificia pūblica ac prīvāta
M-O s.v. national debt: dēbitum pūblicum
terms.comment: Latin says “national” with the state’s own words: pūblicus for what belongs to the whole state, and the people’s own adjective (Rōmānus, Graecus) for what belongs to one nation.

terms.gloss: of one’s own country, native: national (language, customs, songs)
evidence: Curt. 3.3.9: Magī proximī patrium carmen canēbant
terms.comment: Lewis & Short translate Curtius’s patrium carmen “a national song”.

evidence: Cic. Fam. 9.15.2: facētiīs, maximē nostrātibus (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Cicero’s word for what is our own: verba nostrātia, home-grown words (Fam. 2.11.1, Lewis & Short).
Rare and post-Augustan: Tacitus, of a people’s own custom.
Not ancient: classical nātiō is a people or a tribe, and has no adjective.

phrases.latin: Illī rēbus dīvīnīs intersunt, sacrificia pūblica ac prīvāta prōcūrant, religiōnēs interpretantur
phrases.english: They take part in worship, look after the sacrifices of the state and of private people, and interpret religious questions
Next came the Magi, singing their national hymn
